newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to up.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended flat to a touch higher Monday as players braced for Tuesday's data on December consumer prices and retail sales.
"We were trying to hold on to some gains here most of the day," a trader said.
He added that while some bonds managed to preserve 1/8 point gains, most of the market ended unchanged. Some dollar bonds had been up 1/4 of a point at one stage, he said.
A municipal analyst said high-grade issues ended unchanged, while dollar bonds finished flat to up slightly.
Dollars had been up 1/8 point at noon (EST), but faded, he said.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed down 2/32 at 114-8/32. The March T-bond contract closed up 2/32 at 110-13/32. The MOB spread was 123 ticks.
In the government bond cash market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed down 2/32 at 95-17/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
On the economic front, economists polled by Reuters expect CPI to rise 0.3 percent overall, and 0.2 percent in the core rate, which excludes the more volatile food and energy prices.
They expect retail sales to rise by 0.5 percent overall, and by 0.4 percent excluding autos.
Back in municipals, a second municipal analyst said AMG Data Services reported $747 million of outflows from municipal bond funds during the latest reporting week.
While the figure appears large, "a good 80 percent of that is hot money, so there are a lot of market timers, " the analyst said.
"If you kind of correct for hot money, it's really close to maybe $100 million worth of outflows, " he said.

As for the so-called "January effect," the analyst said while some evidence of it has been seen this year, he had expected this year's cash flows to be down about 20 percent versus last year, "basically because there is less stuff rolling off and less stuff maturing, etc," he said.
Never-the-less, "the market certainly has appreciated somewhat at the long end versus mid-December," the analyst said.

Turning to new issues, Tuesday's scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales for are expected to total $557 million in 40 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales are expected to total total $261 million million in 28 sales. The largest is a $90 million Alameda County, Calif., transit deal at 1300 EST.
Negotiated sales are expected to total $296 million in 12 offerings. The largest is a $72.7 million District of Columbia revenue bond deal through Lehman Brothers.
For the week, the biggest competitive deal is a $195 million North Carolina revenue bond offering on Wednesday.
On the negotiated side, a $550 million New York City general obligation deal through Goldman Sachs & Co on Wednesday is the biggest expected sale.

A city official said $65 million of retail orders came in on Monday, bringing total retail orders to $150 million since the order period began Friday. The order period continues Tuesday. No single maturity has sold out so far, the official said.
The second largest negotiated deal is a $423 million Dade County, Fla., offering expected via PaineWebber Inc on Thursday.
